metadata.title: NAP-001: QIAprep Spin Miniprep Kit High-Yield Protocol
metadata.purpose: High-yield purification of up to 30 μg high-copy plasmid DNA from bacterial cultures grown to a high cell density (e.g., culture grown in 5 ml 2x YT medium) using the QIAprep Spin Miniprep Kit (cat. nos. 27104 and 27106).
metadata.scope: This protocol is specially optimized for high-yield purification of high-copy plasmid DNA from bacterial cultures grown to a high cell density. For purification of low-copy plasmids and cosmids, large plasmids (>10 kb), and DNA prepared using other methods, refer to the recommendations in the QIAprep Miniprep Handbook. For further details, including safety information, refer to the QIAprep Miniprep Handbook.
beforeYouBegin: Add LyseBlue reagent to Buffer P1 at a ratio of 1 to 1000.
Add the provided RNase A solution to Buffer P1, mix, and store at 2–8°C.
Add ethanol (96–100%) to Buffer PE before use (see bottle label for volume).
All centrifugation steps, unless stated otherwise, are carried out at 13,000 rpm (~17,900 x g) in a conventional table-top microcentrifuge.

Certain insert–plasmid constructs may reduce the copy number of the plasmid, resulting in lower yields after preparation. In addition, not all E. coli strains are suitable for high-yield plasmid purification. This protocol was verified using E. coli DH5α carrying pCMVβ plasmid.

materials.name: Bacterial strain carrying plasmid of interest
materials.specification: Protocol verified using E. coli DH5α carrying pCMVβ plasmid. Not all E. coli strains are suitable for high-yield plasmid purification.

materials.name: QIAGEN Buffer P1
materials.specification: Add RNase A solution and LyseBlue reagent (1:1000 ratio) before use; store at 2–8°C after addition of RNase A

materials.name: QIAGEN Buffer PB
materials.specification: Contains guanidine hydrochloride, isopropanol: harmful, flammable, irritant

materials.name: QIAGEN Buffer PE
materials.specification: Add ethanol (96–100%) before use (see bottle label for volume)

materials.name: LyseBlue reagent
materials.specification: Add to Buffer P1 at a ratio of 1 to 1000

materials.name: RNase A solution
materials.specification: Provided as a 10 mg/ml solution; add to Buffer P1 before use

materials.specification: User-supplied; add to Buffer PE before use

equipment.name: Conventional table-top microcentrifuge
equipment.settings: Capable of 13,000 rpm (~17,900 x g); also capable of >8000 rpm (6800 x g) for pelleting

equipment.name: Vacuum manifold with luer connectors
equipment.settings: Optional alternative to centrifuge processing for column binding and wash steps (steps 7–9)

samples.name: Bacterial pellet from 5 ml overnight culture in 2x YT medium

tables.title: Yield Comparison: Standard Protocol vs. High-Yield Protocol
tables.note: Values estimated from Figure 1 in the QIAprep Spin Miniprep Kit High-Yield Protocol document. Plasmid DNA was isolated from E. coli DH5α (carrying plasmid pCMVβ) cultured in LB medium or 2x YT medium, using the QIAprep Spin Miniprep standard protocol and the high-yield protocol, respectively.

steps.action: Inoculate 5 ml 2x YT medium with the bacterial strain and incubate the culture for 12–16 h at 37°C. Avoid overgrowth, which may lead to reduced plasmid yields.
steps.criticalNotes: Avoid overgrowth, which may lead to reduced plasmid yields.

steps.action: Pellet 5 ml bacterial overnight culture by centrifugation at >8000 rpm (6800 x g) for 3 min at room temperature (15–25°C).
Completely resuspend pelleted bacterial cells in 250 μl Buffer P1 and transfer to a microcentrifuge tube. Ensure that no clumps of cells remain.
steps.criticalNotes: Ensure that no clumps of cells remain.

steps.action: Add 250 μl Buffer P2 and mix by inverting the tube 10–12 times until the solution turns completely blue. Incubate for 5 min. Do not allow lysis to proceed for more than 5 min.
steps.criticalNotes: Do not allow lysis to proceed for more than 5 min.
steps.expectedResult: The solution turns completely blue (LyseBlue indicator).

steps.action: Add 350 μl Buffer N3 and mix immediately and thoroughly by inverting the tube 10–12 times until the solution turns colorless.
steps.expectedResult: The solution turns colorless (LyseBlue indicator confirms effective SDS precipitation).

parameters.rawText: 13,000 rpm (~17,900 x g) per Notes before starting
~17,900 x g per Notes before starting

steps.action: Apply the supernatant from step 6 to the QIAprep spin column by decanting or pipetting. Centrifuge for 30–60 s and discard the flow-through, or apply vacuum to the manifold to draw the solution through the QIAprep spin column and switch off the vacuum at source.
Wash the QIAprep spin column by adding 500 μl Buffer PB. Centrifuge as in step 7, or apply vacuum to draw the solution through the QIAprep spin column as in step 7.

Wash the QIAprep spin column by adding 750 μl Buffer PE. Centrifuge as in step 7, or apply vacuum to draw the solution through the QIAprep spin column as in step 7. Transfer the QIAprep spin column to the collection tube.
Centrifuge for 1 min to remove residual wash buffer.

Place the QIAprep spin column in a clean 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube. To elute DNA, add 60 μl Buffer EB (10 mM Tris·Cl, pH 8.5) to the center of the QIAprep spin column, let it stand for 1 min, and centrifuge for 1 min.

materialUses.rawText: 60 μl Buffer EB (10 mM Tris·Cl, pH 8.5)

parameters.rawText: 60 μl Buffer EB (10 mM Tris·Cl, pH 8.5)

steps.expectedResult: Eluted plasmid DNA in 60 μl Buffer EB.

steps.action: Measure concentration and purity ratios (A260/A280, A260/A230). Store DNA at –20°C when eluted with water, as DNA may degrade in the absence of a buffering agent.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Expected plasmid A260/A280 is often near 1.8.
Up to 30 μg plasmid DNA from 5 ml 2x YT culture of high-copy plasmid.

steps.criticalNotes: Store DNA at –20°C when eluted with water, as DNA may degrade in the absence of a buffering agent. Elution efficiency is dependent on pH. The maximum elution efficiency is achieved between pH 7.0 and 8.5.

sourceReferences.location: Elution notes, p. 17; DNA yield, p. 12

controls.name: Agarose gel analysis of eluted plasmid DNA
controls.description: The QIAprep Miniprep procedure can be analyzed using agarose gel electrophoresis. The eluted pure plasmid DNA should show no contamination with other nucleic acids. Samples can also be taken from the cleared lysate and its flow-through for comparison.
controls.notes: Source high-yield protocol document does not include explicit control requirements. Agarose gel analysis is described in the QIAprep Miniprep Handbook Appendix B.

controls.name: Diagnostic restriction digest or sequencing for new clones
controls.description: Run a diagnostic restriction digest or Sanger sequencing across insert/junctions for new clones to verify plasmid identity and integrity.
controls.notes: Source high-yield protocol document does not include explicit control requirements. This is standard practice for plasmid miniprep quality control.

expectedOutputs: Up to 30 μg purified high-copy plasmid DNA from 5 ml 2x YT overnight culture.
Higher plasmid DNA yields from cultures grown in 2x YT medium and isolated using the high-yield protocol compared to LB medium with the standard protocol.
Plasmid DNA suitable for restriction enzyme digestion, sequencing, ligation and transformation, library screening, in vitro translation, and transfection of robust cells.

troubleshooting.problem: Low or no yield (general)
troubleshooting.cause: Low yields may be caused by a number of factors.
troubleshooting.solution: To find the source of the problem, analyze fractions saved from each step in the procedure on an agarose gel. A small amount of the cleared lysate and the entire flow-through can be precipitated by adding 0.7 volumes isopropanol and centrifuging at maximum speed (13,000 rpm or ~17,000 x g) for 30 minutes. The entire wash flow-through can be precipitated by adding 0.1 volumes of 3 M sodium acetate, pH 5.0, and 0.7 volumes of isopropanol.

troubleshooting.problem: No DNA in the cleared lysate before loading — plasmid did not propagate
troubleshooting.solution: Read 'Growth of bacterial cultures' (pages 39–41) and check that the conditions for optimal growth were met.

troubleshooting.problem: No DNA in the cleared lysate before loading — lysate prepared incorrectly
troubleshooting.solution: Check storage conditions and age of buffers.

troubleshooting.problem: No DNA in the cleared lysate before loading — Buffer P2 precipitated
troubleshooting.solution: Redissolve by warming to 37°C.

troubleshooting.problem: No DNA in the cleared lysate before loading — cell resuspension incomplete
troubleshooting.solution: Pelleted cells should be completely resuspended in Buffer P1. Do not add Buffer P2 until an even suspension is obtained.

troubleshooting.problem: DNA is found in the flow-through of cleared lysate
troubleshooting.solution: If rich culture media, such as TB or 2x YT are used, culture volumes must be reduced. It may be necessary to adjust LB culture volume if the plasmid and host strain show extremely high copy number or growth rates. See 'Culture media' on page 41.

troubleshooting.problem: Low or no yield — RNase A digestion omitted
troubleshooting.solution: Ensure that RNase A is added to Buffer P1 before use.

troubleshooting.problem: Low or no yield — RNase A digestion insufficient
troubleshooting.solution: Reduce culture volume if necessary. If Buffer P1 containing RNase A is more than 6 months old, add additional RNase A.

troubleshooting.problem: DNA is found in the wash flow-through
troubleshooting.cause: Ethanol omitted from wash buffer (Buffer PE).
troubleshooting.solution: Repeat procedure with correctly prepared wash buffer (Buffer PE).

troubleshooting.problem: Little or no DNA in eluate — elution buffer incorrect
troubleshooting.solution: DNA is eluted only in the presence of low-salt buffer (e.g., Buffer EB [10 mM Tris·Cl, pH 8.5] or water). Elution efficiency is dependent on pH. The maximum elution efficiency is achieved between pH 7.0 and 8.5. When using water for elution, make sure that the pH value is within this range.

troubleshooting.problem: Little or no DNA in eluate — elution buffer incorrectly dispensed onto membrane
troubleshooting.cause: Elution buffer incorrectly dispensed onto membrane.
troubleshooting.solution: Add elution buffer to the center of the QIAprep membrane to ensure that the buffer completely covers the surface of the membrane for maximum elution efficiency.

troubleshooting.problem: Low DNA quality — eluate salt concentration too high
troubleshooting.solution: For the QIAprep spin column, modify the wash step by incubating the column for 5 minutes at room temperature after adding 0.75 ml of Buffer PE and then centrifuging. For QIAprep 8 preparations and QIAprep 8 and 96 Turbo preparations, ensure that two wash steps are carried out prior to elution.

troubleshooting.problem: Low DNA quality — nuclease contamination
troubleshooting.solution: When using endA+ host strains such as HB101 and its derivatives, the JM series, or any wild-type strain, ensure that the wash step with Buffer PB is performed.

troubleshooting.problem: Low DNA quality — eluate contains residual ethanol
troubleshooting.solution: Ensure that the additional centrifugation step to remove residual wash buffer (step 10 in the high-yield protocol) is performed.

troubleshooting.problem: RNA in the eluate — RNase A digestion omitted
troubleshooting.solution: Ensure that RNase A is added to Buffer P1 before use.

troubleshooting.problem: RNA in the eluate — RNase A digestion insufficient
troubleshooting.solution: Reduce culture volume if necessary. If Buffer P1 containing RNase A is more than 6 months old, add additional RNase A.

troubleshooting.problem: Genomic DNA in the eluate — Buffer P2 added incorrectly
troubleshooting.solution: The lysate must be handled gently after addition of Buffer P2 to prevent shearing. Reduce culture volume if lysate is too viscous for gentle mixing.

troubleshooting.problem: Genomic DNA in the eluate — Buffer N3 added incorrectly
troubleshooting.solution: Upon addition of Buffer N3 in step 5, mix immediately but gently.

troubleshooting.problem: Genomic DNA in the eluate — lysis too long
troubleshooting.solution: Lysis in step 4 must not exceed 5 minutes.

troubleshooting.problem: Genomic DNA in the eluate — culture overgrown
troubleshooting.solution: Overgrown cultures contain lysed cells and degraded DNA. Do not grow cultures for longer than 12–16 hours.

safety: When working with chemicals, always wear a suitable lab coat, disposable gloves, and protective goggles. For more information, please consult the appropriate material safety data sheets (MSDSs).
CAUTION: DO NOT add bleach or acidic solutions directly to the sample-preparation waste.
Buffers N3 and PB contain guanidine hydrochloride, which can form highly reactive compounds when combined with bleach.

If liquid containing these buffers is spilt, clean with suitable laboratory detergent and water. If the spilt liquid contains potentially infectious agents, clean the affected area first with laboratory detergent and water, and then with 1% (v/v) sodium hypochlorite.
Buffer N3: Contains guanidine hydrochloride, acetic acid: harmful, irritant. Risk and safety phrases: R22-36/38, S13-23-26-36/37/39-46.
Buffer P2: Contains sodium hydroxide: irritant. Risk and safety phrases: R36/38, S13-26-36-46.
Buffer PB: Contains guanidine hydrochloride, isopropanol: harmful, flammable, irritant. Risk and safety phrases: R10-22-36/38, S13-23-26-36/37/39-46.
RNase A: Contains ribonuclease: sensitizer. Risk and safety phrases: R42/43, S23-24-26-36/37.
